problem_title: Broken Hand Pump in Village
problem_description: The only community hand pump in Rampur village, Bihar, has been non-functional for 3 months. Residents (≈500 people) walk 4 km daily for water. District administration has not responded to two written complaints.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Safe drinking water is a flagship national priority (Jal Jeevan Mission). Direct alignment.
Repair falls under district panchayat mandate; standard process exists but complaints were ignored, indicating friction.
Hand pump repair is a well-understood, low-cost operation. Materials are locally available.
500 people without water; health risk is high. Breadth and depth of impact are both significant.
Three months without primary water source. Health and hygiene emergency.

problem_title: Pothole-Riddled State Highway Near School
problem_description: A 2 km stretch of SH-47 in Rajasthan near a government school has 60+ potholes. Two road accidents in the last month. School buses are rerouting, adding 20 minutes per trip. PWD raised request 8 months ago; no action.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Road maintenance is a core PWD mandate; school proximity adds child safety angle.
Approval chain exists but 8-month delay shows bureaucratic friction. Procurement may take time.
Pothole patching is a routine civil works activity; contractors are available.
Accidents recorded; school children affected. Impact is real but geographically limited to 2 km stretch.
Two accidents already; monsoon season will worsen road condition rapidly.

problem_title: No Street Lights on Night Market Road
problem_description: A 1.5 km road in Pune's weekly night market has no functional street lighting. Three mugging incidents reported to police in two months. 300+ vendors operate here nightly.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Safety infrastructure is a local body responsibility; relevant but not a national flagship scheme.
Street light installation falls clearly under municipal corporation MLALAD/ward fund.
Solar street lights can be deployed quickly; no major civil works required.
300 vendors and their customers affected nightly; security risk is real and documented.
Three muggings in two months; situation likely to worsen without intervention.

problem_title: Garbage Accumulation in Urban Slum
problem_description: Ward 12, Bhopal has not had waste collection for 45 days. Five metric tonnes of garbage accumulating near a school and maternity centre. Rats and stray dogs are breeding in the waste.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Swachh Bharat Mission directly addresses urban solid waste; near school and maternity centre adds urgency.
Municipal waste collection is routine; the lapse suggests contractor or administrative failure requiring escalation.
Deploying a waste collection vehicle is operationally straightforward; one-time clearance is feasible.
Health risk to children and pregnant women; disease vector breeding site. High impact.
45 days lapse; active disease risk. Immediate action required.

problem_title: Request for Heritage Tourism Signage
problem_description: A local cultural society wants bilingual heritage tourism signboards installed at 12 heritage sites in a tier-3 city. Current signs are only in English and are 20 years old.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Tourism development is a state priority but signage renewal is low-priority relative to active services.
Tourism department has a standard signage budget; DAST scheme applies.
Signboard fabrication and installation is trivial civil work.
Visitors benefit but does not address a citizen welfare need; impact is cultural, not urgent.
No safety or health risk; low urgency.

problem_title: No Cold Storage Near Mango Belt
problem_description: Farmers in the Malda mango belt (West Bengal) lose 40% of produce annually due to absence of cold storage within 30 km. Average farm income loss per family is ₹18,000/year.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Cold storage using solar-powered refrigeration is mature technology. Off-the-shelf solutions exist.
Model is replicable across fruit belts; standardised design scales to other districts.
Cold storage is not novel; incremental innovation possible with IoT monitoring and last-mile logistics.
Cold storage capex is significant (₹1–3 Cr per unit); grants and NABARD financing exist but cost is real.
Agri-cold-chain is a growing market; value-add for exports and domestic processing.

problem_title: Open Defecation Due to Lack of Toilets in Construction Sites
problem_description: 400+ construction workers on a Nagpur highway project have no access to toilet facilities. Open defecation near water bodies and village outskirts is causing community complaints.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Portable bio-toilets are mature, available, and low-maintenance. No technology barrier.
Same model applies to all construction sites; regulation can scale deployment.
No significant innovation opportunity; standard compliance solution.
Mobile toilet units are low-cost to deploy and operate; rental models exist.
Rental sanitation market exists but is niche; main driver is regulatory compliance, not market opportunity.

problem_title: No Digital Payment Option at Village Weekly Market
problem_description: A weekly haat in Jharkhand with 800 vendors cannot accept digital payments due to no network coverage and no QR infrastructure. Cash losses to theft are common. Vendors request low-cost digital payment support.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Offline UPI and USSD payment tech exists but requires device rollout and network improvements; feasible but with friction.
Rural digital payment infrastructure is a national-scale problem; solution is highly replicable.
Offline payment stack, mesh networking for low-connectivity areas presents real innovation opportunity.
Device cost is moderate; network infrastructure improvement is expensive; government subsidy schemes exist.
Fintech companies actively targeting rural B2B2C market; strong commercial interest.

problem_title: Pesticide Residue in Groundwater Near Industrial Estate
problem_description: Borewells in 3 villages near a Ludhiana industrial estate test positive for heavy metals (chromium, lead). Source traced to effluent discharge from a cluster of electroplating units. Villagers report skin and stomach ailments.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Effluent treatment plants (ETP) for electroplating are available; compliance technology is known.
Common ETP model for industrial clusters is replicable but requires sustained enforcement.
Advanced oxidation, bioremediation of heavy metals could be an R&D opportunity; not mainstream yet.
ETP installation is capital-intensive; small units in informal clusters typically cannot bear the cost without pooling and subsidy.
Environmental services market exists; PCPCR compliance creates demand. Limited commercial upside for SMEs.

problem_title: Request for Silicon Valley-Style Co-Working Space in Tier-2 City
problem_description: A startup group requests a government-funded premium co-working space in Indore with high-speed fibre, conference rooms, and mentorship programmes.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Co-working spaces are mature; fibre internet and shared infrastructure are readily available.
Model is replicable across tier-2 cities; existing examples from iCreate, T-Hub.
Innovation ecosystem value is indirect; facility itself is not novel.
Real-estate and fit-out costs in a tier-2 city are moderate; government land allocation reduces cost.
Growing startup density in tier-2 cities; ancillary services market developing.

problem_title: Inadequate STEM Labs in Rural Government Schools
problem_description: 80% of government schools in Bastar, Chhattisgarh, lack basic science lab equipment. Students cannot perform mandatory practical examinations. Pass rates in science are 40% lower than state average.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Pedagogical research consistently shows lab-based learning improves STEM outcomes. Scientifically sound.
Excellent case study for low-cost STEM pedagogy, curriculum adaptation for tribal/rural contexts, and learning outcome measurement.
Low-cost lab kits, virtual labs, and mobile lab vans present real innovation opportunities.
Lab setup is a well-understood intervention. No scientific uncertainty.
Literature on rural STEM gaps exists; local context adaptation is under-studied.

problem_title: Antibiotic Resistant Bacteria in Hospital Effluent
problem_description: Samples from a hospital waste water treatment plant in Lucknow show high concentrations of antibiotic-resistant E. coli and Klebsiella. The treated effluent is discharged into a river used for irrigation.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: AMR in hospital effluent is a scientifically documented, high-priority global health risk.
High-impact research area: AMR surveillance, advanced treatment (UV, ozone), epidemiology, one-health models.
Novel treatment technologies, genomic surveillance, real-time monitoring are active research frontiers.
Some treatment methods are proven; full AMR elimination in effluent is scientifically challenging.
Hospital effluent AMR in India is critically under-monitored; surveillance data is scarce.

problem_title: Students Without Drinking Water in College Hostel
problem_description: A state university hostel in Odisha has no functional water purifier. 400 students drink untreated borewell water. Two cases of typhoid reported last semester.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Waterborne disease from untreated groundwater is scientifically established.
Low research potential — standard public health problem with well-known solutions.
No novel research opportunity; procurement/administration problem.
RO/UV purification is fully proven technology.
No meaningful knowledge gap; solution is known.

problem_title: No Earthquake Early Warning System in Himalayan Foothills
problem_description: Towns in the seismically active Garhwal region (Uttarakhand) have no earthquake early warning infrastructure. The nearest seismic station is 150 km away. Building codes are frequently violated.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Seismic early warning systems are scientifically validated; Mexico, Japan deployments demonstrate effectiveness.
Himalayas are highly complex seismic zones. Research in local attenuation, site effects, warning algorithm calibration is needed.
IoT seismic sensor mesh, ML-based P-wave detection, hyperlocal warnings are active R&D areas.
Warning time is limited (seconds) in near-field events; scientific challenge is real but tractable.
Himalayan seismic hazard is under-instrumented and under-modelled. Significant gaps.

problem_title: No Science Teacher for 3 Years in Tribal Block School
problem_description: A government higher secondary school in a Naxal-affected Dantewada block has had no permanent science teacher for 3 years. Students are self-studying for board exams.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Teacher shortage impact on learning outcomes is empirically established.
Moderate: research on remote/conflict-area teaching delivery, digital-first pedagogy for underserved students.
AI tutoring, asynchronous video lessons, peer learning models are innovation opportunities.
Digital content delivery is technically proven even in low-bandwidth environments.
Pedagogy for conflict-affected tribal zones is under-researched in Indian context.

problem_title: Public Toilet Locked at Night in Railway Station Area
problem_description: The only public toilet block near Jhansi railway station is locked between 10 PM and 6 AM by the contractor. Passengers and daily-wage workers resort to open defecation. Women feel particularly unsafe.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Basic sanitation access at night is fundamental; safety risk for women is a critical concern.
Railway area has high daily footfall; open defecation affects dignity, health, and safety directly.
Ongoing nightly problem affecting commuters and residents every day.
Solution (extend operating hours, digital lock) is simple and low-cost; immediately actionable by citizens.
Guaranteed improvement in dignity, hygiene, and safety at negligible cost if operating hours are extended.

problem_title: No Bus Service to Village After 6 PM
problem_description: Sundarnagar village, HP, has no bus service after 6 PM. Workers at a factory 15 km away must walk or pay ₹200 for auto-rickshaws daily. Monthly transport cost exceeds ₹5,000 for a low-wage worker.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Transport poverty directly limits economic participation and livelihood. High importance for affected families.
₹5,000/month transport cost on a low wage is severe. Safety risk of night walking also real.
Ongoing problem but not an acute emergency; workers have adapted (at high personal cost).
Bus schedule extension requires HRTC approval; not complex but requires persistent advocacy.
Evening bus service would save ₹4,000+/month per worker and eliminate nightly safety risk.

problem_title: Ration Shop Opens Only 2 Days Per Month
problem_description: The PDS ration shop in Ward 7, Gwalior opens only on the 1st and 15th of each month for 3 hours. Elderly and disabled residents miss their quota. Shopkeeper reports stock arrives late.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Food security through PDS is a legal right. Denial is both a welfare and rights issue.
Elderly and disabled citizens are systematically excluded due to limited access hours; direct deprivation.
Food insecurity is inherently urgent; recurrent monthly problem compounds harm.
Complaints can be filed with food inspector but institutional response is slow; digital PDS portals are inaccessible to this demographic.
Regular opening times would immediately ensure every eligible citizen receives their legal entitlement.

problem_title: Slow WiFi at Common Service Centre (CSC)
problem_description: The only CSC in a block of 12,000 residents has a 2 Mbps connection. Citizens wait 45+ minutes per transaction (Aadhaar update, certificate applications). Operator charges ₹50 extra for priority service.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: CSC access is critical for government service delivery; slow connection impedes official transactions.
45-minute wait per visit and informal charges impose time and financial burden on citizens.
Inconvenient but not a health or safety risk; services are eventually accessible.
BBNL upgrade requests must go through district NIC; process is slow and opaque for citizens.
10–20 Mbps upgrade would cut wait times to under 5 minutes; straightforward improvement.

problem_title: No Anganwadi Centre for Remote Hamlet
problem_description: Hamlets of Telidih and Hatia (combined population 340) in Jharkhand have no Anganwadi within 5 km. Children under 5 and pregnant women miss ICDS nutritional supplementation.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Under-5 nutrition and maternal health are fundamental; ICDS is a constitutional commitment.
Children and pregnant women in vulnerable communities are denied supplemental nutrition; severe long-term consequences.
Malnutrition damage is cumulative; every month of gap worsens developmental outcomes.
Requesting new Anganwadi requires district ICDS approval and budget; process is slow.
Anganwadi centre would immediately address nutrition gap for the most vulnerable population.

problem_title: River Pollution from Festival Idol Immersion
problem_description: The Ganga bank near Patna experiences severe water quality degradation after Durga Puja and Ganesh Chaturthi immersions (plaster of Paris, synthetic dyes). Fishing community of 2,000 reports reduced catch for 3 months post-festival.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: 2,000 fisherfolk livelihood affected; river is also drinking source for downstream villages.
Fishing community expresses strong need; water quality affects livelihood and health.
Marginalised fishing community (often SC/ST) disproportionately impacted; solution must protect their livelihood.
Eco-friendly idols are gaining acceptance but cultural resistance to change is real; community engagement required.
Eco-friendly idol movement is growing; long-term cultural shift is achievable with sustained advocacy.

problem_title: No Community Hall for Village Events and Disaster Shelter
problem_description: A village of 1,800 in Odisha's coastal belt has no community hall. During cyclone warnings, residents shelter in a structurally unsafe school building. Village gatherings happen outdoors regardless of weather.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Dual function: regular community cohesion and emergency shelter. High social value.
Community unanimously expresses need; cyclone risk makes shelter infrastructure critical.
Accessible infrastructure benefits all including elderly, disabled, and women during disasters.
Community has already mobilised for land; high ownership of the project.
MGNREGA, PMAY-G, or PMGSY funding routes exist; maintenance requires panchayat ownership.

problem_title: Youth Migrating Out Due to No Livelihood in Village
problem_description: 90% of youth aged 18–30 in Tikamgarh block, MP, migrate to cities for construction work. Village population is ageing. Traditional crafts (terracotta, weaving) are dying out as no market linkage exists.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Youth outmigration hollows out villages; elderly left behind without support. Craft heritage loss is irreversible.
Remaining community members express strong desire to retain youth; intergenerational fabric at risk.
Women artisans are primary craft keepers; solution should prioritise their market access.
Youth may return only if income parity with city is close; partial adoption likely initially.
Market linkage through GI tagging, e-commerce is viable but requires sustained intervention and quality standards.

problem_title: Stray Dog Menace in Urban Locality
problem_description: Residents of a Bengaluru locality report 15+ dog bite incidents in 6 months. BBMP's ABC (Animal Birth Control) programme has not visited in 2 years. Children and elderly residents are afraid to step outside.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Dog bites cause physical harm and restrict movement; public health risk (rabies) is real.
Residents urgently express need for ABC programme; safety is a basic expectation.
Children and elderly are most vulnerable; solution must consider their mobility needs.
Community is strongly supportive of ABC; humane animal management is culturally acceptable in urban context.
ABC is a recurring BBMP duty; without sustained programme, problem will recur.

problem_title: Disputed Common Land Encroachment in Tribal Village
problem_description: 400 acres of forest-fringe common land in a Bastar tribal village are being encroached by private parties. Tribal families depend on this land for minor forest produce (MFP) — their primary livelihood. FIRs filed but no action in 18 months.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Loss of common land destroys the livelihood base of a tribal community; generational impact.
Tribal community is in active distress; MFP collection is primary income; urgency is high.
ST community is one of the most marginalised groups; solution must directly protect their PESA/FRA rights.
Community is unified and already fighting through legal channels; strong ownership.
Legal recognition of community rights under FRA would provide permanent protection; long process but durable.

problem_title: Inadequate Evidence — Vague Infrastructure Request
problem_description: Residents request 'infrastructure improvement' for their area. No specific problem, no location, no affected population count.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: No specific policy hook identifiable from vague description.
Cannot plan administrative action without knowing the specific need.
Unfeasible to implement without a defined problem.
No evidence of affected population or nature of impact.
No urgency information provided whatsoever.

problem_title: Insufficient Evidence — Industrial Innovation Request
problem_description: A group claims 'industry needs help' in their region. No sector, no scale, no specific problem described.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Cannot assess technical feasibility without knowing what is being built.
No basis to assess scale.
No problem defined; no innovation target.
Cost is completely indeterminate.
No market context provided.

problem_title: Contradictory Information — School Flood Claim
problem_description: A school reportedly flooded every monsoon, but location is described as a plateau with no rivers within 50 km. No photographic or official record provided.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Claimed phenomenon contradicts described geography; scientific validity is questionable without evidence.
If true, it could indicate unusual local drainage; but data is insufficient to assess research potential.
Cannot identify innovation opportunity without verified problem.
Water management for plateaus is feasible but location claim requires verification.
Cannot identify knowledge gaps from contradictory claims.

problem_title: Adversarial — Claims Government Owes Free Luxury Housing
problem_description: Submitter demands that the government provide free 3BHK flats with AC to all citizens as their constitutional right, citing a fabricated Supreme Court order. No authentic reference provided.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Housing demand is real in principle, but the specific claim is unrealistic and appears adversarial/fabricated.
No genuine user welfare problem is described beyond a legally unsupported entitlement claim.
No urgency demonstrated.
Proposed solution (free luxury flats for all) is not a governance-feasible intervention.
Proposal as stated would not improve systemic welfare; it is not a legitimate policy ask.

problem_title: Adversarial — Community Demands Removal of All Factories
problem_description: Residents demand immediate closure of all industries within 50 km 'because pollution exists', without citing specific violations, measurement data, or legal violations.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Pollution concern is legitimate in principle but the demand as stated is disproportionate and unsupported by evidence.
Community desire for clean air is a genuine need; but specific polluters and violations must be identified.
Factory closures would also harm workers and dependent communities; the framing ignores inclusive impact.
Extreme demand is unlikely to result in policy change; actionable solutions (monitoring, compliance) would achieve more.
Blanket closure is not sustainable; a regulated industrial ecosystem is the appropriate goal.

problem_title: Flood-Damaged Primary School in UP
problem_description: Kamla Primary School in Lakhimpur Kheri, UP was partially damaged by floods in August. Two classrooms have collapsed roof sections. 280 students are studying under a tarpaulin. Collector has acknowledged damage in a report dated 3 months ago.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: School reconstruction after disaster is covered under NDRF and SDP funds; high alignment with Samagra Shiksha guidelines.
Collector acknowledgement means the problem is already in the system; NDRF claim process is defined.
Classroom repair is standard civil work; contractors available in district.
280 students affected; education continuity, health risk from open-air schooling in upcoming winter.
3 months elapsed with acknowledgement but no action; winter approaching. Urgent.

problem_title: High Incidence of Workplace Injuries in SSI Foundries
problem_description: Small foundries in Kolhapur, Maharashtra report 12% annual injury rate among contract workers — 3× the national manufacturing average. No safety audits conducted in 5 years. Workers lack PPE.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: PPE, safety interlocks, sensor-based hazard detection are mature and affordable for SMEs.
Safety intervention model is replicable across SSI foundry clusters nationwide.
Wearable safety monitoring, AI accident prediction could be applied; incremental innovation.
Basic PPE and safety training are low-cost; audit framework requires some investment.
Industrial safety services market is growing; insurance industry creates commercial incentive.

problem_title: Recurring Malaria Cluster in Tribal Area
problem_description: A tribal block in Bastar records 600–800 malaria cases annually with 3–5 deaths. Plasmodium falciparum (severe form) is predominant. Standard treatment is available but vector control (IRS, bednet distribution) is inconsistent.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Malaria biology, drug treatment, and vector control are thoroughly established.
Drug resistance monitoring, local vector behaviour, ethnobotanical remedies, community health worker models for remote areas.
Gene drive, spatial repellents, AI-based surveillance of breeding sites are active research areas.
IRS and bednet distribution are proven; implementation gap, not scientific gap.
Local vector resistance profiles, treatment compliance in tribal populations — specific data gaps exist.

problem_title: Delayed Pension for Senior Citizen
problem_description: A 72-year-old widow in Nagpur has not received her NSAP pension for 6 months due to a bank account linkage error. She has visited the block office 4 times. Each visit results in a different reason for the delay.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Pension is the sole income for a 72-year-old widow; denial causes severe financial and psychological distress.
Six months without income at age 72; direct daily life impact is extreme.
Every week of delay compounds harm for an elderly, economically vulnerable person.
Online grievance portal exists but is inaccessible to an elderly person without smartphone literacy; in-person process is failing.
Correcting the bank linkage is a simple administrative fix; restoration is immediate once done.

problem_title: Defunct Self Help Group — Loan Not Recovered
problem_description: A 12-member women's SHG in Vidarbha stopped functioning after the president migrated. ₹2.3 lakh in undisbursed NRLM funds are held in escrow. Remaining members want to reconstitute and restart.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Women's SHGs are proven community welfare instruments; reconstitution would restore collective benefit.
Remaining members are motivated and express clear need; economic and social support function is lost.
Women, particularly in Vidarbha's agrarian distress context, are among the most vulnerable; SHG is a proven inclusion tool.
Existing members want to restart; leadership gap is the only barrier.
NRLM framework provides long-term support structure; once reconstituted, survival probability is good.

problem_title: Clogged Drainage Causing Waterlogging in Colony
problem_description: Colony in Pune with 2,000 residents experiences waterlogging every monsoon. Main drain clogged for 3 years. Residents' cars and property regularly flooded. Corporation has received 40+ complaints.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Urban flood management is part of Smart City / AMRUT programmes; routine municipal duty.
Should be straightforward PMC work but 3-year backlog suggests contractor/budget/priority issue.
Drain desilting/unblocking is standard maintenance; no complex engineering required.
2,000 residents; property damage and waterborne disease risk every year.
Annual recurring event; monsoon is predictable. Pre-monsoon action is clearly needed.

problem_title: MSME Cluster Cannot Access Export Market Due to Certification Gap
problem_description: A cluster of 80 MSMEs making handloom silk products in Varanasi cannot export because they lack BIS/CE certifications. Cluster collective turnover is ₹12 crore/year. Export potential estimated at ₹3× domestic.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Certification processes are well-defined; technical requirements for handloom are moderate.
Model applicable to all textile MSME clusters facing export certification barriers; replicable nationwide.
Little innovation opportunity in a certification compliance problem; value is in access, not innovation.
Certification cost is significant per MSME but shared cluster certification reduces individual burden.
₹36 crore export potential from a single cluster; Varanasi silk is globally recognised brand.

problem_title: High Dropout Rate in Girls' Education in Border District
problem_description: A border district in Rajasthan has 55% dropout rate for girls after Class 8. Reasons include distance to secondary school (10+ km), early marriage pressure, no female teachers. State average is 22%.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Barriers to female secondary education are well-documented; evidence base is strong.
Localized intervention research: residential school models, mobile education units, female mentor networks, socio-economic impact studies.
AI-based personalised learning, remote tutoring, community radio for education are applicable innovations.
Proven interventions exist (Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya, etc.); feasibility is established.
Border district dynamics, cross-border migration effects on female education — some context gaps.

problem_title: Hospital Charges Extra for BPL Card Patients
problem_description: A government district hospital in Bihar charges BPL card holders unofficial fees for lab tests covered under PMJAY. Patients are told 'machine is broken' when they refuse to pay. Three families report being turned away.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Denial of free healthcare to BPL families is a violation of a legal entitlement; deeply harmful.
Poorest families denied health services; direct harm to health and financial security.
Health-related rights violations need immediate redress; delay causes ongoing harm.
PMJAY grievance portal exists but is unknown to and inaccessible for illiterate rural BPL cardholders.
Strict vigilance/audit would immediately restore legal entitlement; high improvement if enforcement acts.

problem_title: Seasonal Worker Housing in Sugarcane Harvest Season
problem_description: 20,000 migrant workers arrive annually in Solapur for sugarcane cutting. Contractors provide no proper housing; workers sleep in fields or makeshift shelters. No sanitation, no safe water. Children travel with parents; no school access.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Massive scale (20,000 workers + families); multi-dimensional deprivation of housing, water, sanitation, education.
Acute, recurring need; workers are among the most economically vulnerable in the agricultural labour force.
Seasonal migrants are invisible in administrative systems; children face loss of school year annually.
Workers would accept any improvement; contractor compliance requires enforcement and incentive.
Seasonal worker welfare codes exist under CLRA; enforcement is the gap; structural change requires sustained policy.

problem_title: Hinglish Short Description — Bus Stand Needs Repair
problem_description: Yahaan ka bus stand bahut purana hai, log baarish mein bheegte hain. Koi shelter nahi. Sarkaar ko sudhaarna chahiye.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Bus shelter maintenance is a local transport authority duty; modest national relevance.
Standard PWD/urban body civil works; budget allocation for bus shelters is routine.
Shelter construction or prefab canopy installation is simple civil work.
Commuters benefit; scope is local. No health or safety emergency.
Inconvenient but not urgent; monsoon season adds discomfort but no danger.

problem_title: Hinglish — Paani nahi aata
problem_description: Hamare mohalle mein teen din se paani nahi aaya. Tanker maangne par bola gaya 'kal aayega'. Do pregnant mahilayein hain ghar mein.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Three days without water with pregnant women is a health emergency.
Pregnant women and all household members at risk; immediate daily-life disruption.
Three days is critical; pregnancy makes the situation a medical emergency.
Tanker requested but delayed; escalation path (ward officer, helpline) may not be known to residents.
A single tanker dispatch would immediately relieve the crisis.

problem_title: Cross-Domain — Waterlogging Destroying Crops and Homes
problem_description: Recurring waterlogging in Sitamarhi, Bihar affects 800 families. 30% of paddy crop is lost annually. Two families lost their mud homes to seepage collapse. Children miss school during flood weeks.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Crop loss, home loss, and school disruption across 800 families. Multi-dimensional severe impact.
Community has been suffering recurring losses for years; urgent collective need.
Marginal farmers and families with mud homes are most vulnerable to waterlogging; poorest are hardest hit.
Community is motivated to solve; collective drainage improvement has precedents in Bihar.
Drainage improvement is durable; MGNREGA and RKVY funds available for agricultural land drainage.

problem_title: Cross-Domain — Tourism Waste Destroying Biodiversity
problem_description: High tourist footfall in a biodiversity hotspot in Coorg has increased plastic waste 4× in 3 years. Local homestay operators report revenue loss as wildlife sightings drop. Forest department has no enforcement capacity.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Plastic waste management technology (collection, recycling, bio-degradables) is available; deployment in remote areas has friction.
Eco-tourism waste management model applicable to all protected areas facing similar pressure.
Biodegradable packaging, deposit-return systems, AI-based litter monitoring are applicable innovations.
Waste management infrastructure in biodiversity-sensitive areas is expensive; requires specialised equipment.
Ecotourism is premium market; operators have financial incentive to invest in sustainable practices to protect revenue.

problem_title: Long Description — Comprehensive Urban Air Quality Problem
problem_description: Air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR) during October–February reaches AQI levels consistently above 400 (hazardous). Primary contributors: stubble burning from Punjab/Haryana (28%), vehicular emissions (38%), construction dust (18%), industrial sources (16%). SAFAR monitoring data from 2018–2023 shows no improvement in PM2.5 annual average. Health impact: 3,000 excess deaths/year (IHME estimate), 15% increased ER visits for respiratory conditions. Economic cost: ₹5,200 crore annually in productivity loss. Existing interventions: GRAP, OE scheme (odd-even), BS-VI fuel transition, stubble management subsidy. GRAP implementation is inconsistent; farmers cite subsidy inadequacy as barrier to alternative stubble management.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: Extremely well-documented multi-pollutant problem with strong IHME, SAFAR, IIT Delhi data. Causation and health burden are scientifically established.
Source apportionment, intervention effectiveness, health equity, climate co-benefits, agri-economic incentives for stubble management — enormous research portfolio.
Stubble-to-biogas conversion, low-cost sensor networks, hyperlocal pollution forecasting, real-time GRAP optimization.
Technology and knowledge exist; systemic and political barriers are the primary gap.
Indoor-outdoor exposure equity, second-order health effects, multi-city comparative studies — gaps remain despite substantial literature.

problem_title: Cross-Pool — Groundwater Depletion Affecting Borewells
problem_description: Five neighbourhoods in Chennai report borewells failing as water table drops from 30 ft to 80+ ft in 4 years. 1,200 families on borewell dependency have no alternative. Apartment builders continue constructing without borewell impact assessment.

expected_criterion_scores.rationale: 1,200 families losing primary water source. Groundwater depletion is irreversible on short timescales.
Daily water access disrupted; no affordable alternative for residents on borewell.
Table dropping 50 ft in 4 years signals rapid depletion; will worsen with each dry season.
Regulation of apartment builders requires civic body action; individual residents have very limited ability to address structural cause.
Rainwater harvesting mandates, recharge pits, and building approvals with groundwater assessment would stabilise depletion.
